name: Reggie Turner
bio: An old friend of Robert Ross who, in Ross's words, 'had been very kind to Mr Wilde since his release', and the constant presence of Wilde's last weeks at the Hôtel d'Alsace: he sent Ross daily bulletins, was with Wilde 'the whole of the last week of his life', slept at the hotel to give the 4 a.m. remedies, restrained him in delirium, held the ice-bag, and told the doctor he would be responsible for any expenses. He and Ross were, per the editors' plate caption, 'the two friends who were with Oscar on the day he died' (30 November 1900); he walked in the funeral procession and sent a wreath. Wilde's register toward him stayed teasing-affectionate to the end - 'You dear little Jew, don't you think that's enough?' during the ice-bag nursing, and the Rome 1900 photograph sent to Turner inscribed 'A young unmitred Bishop in partibus'. The 1898-99 letters show the ordinary setting of the friendship: Wilde's standing sign-off to him was 'Ever affectionately yours' (p. 1118), and Turner is the correspondent to whom Wilde reports other men's boys, other men's infatuations and a blackmail arrest in a shared idiom that assumes no explanation (pp. 1107-1108, 1122). Looking back on Berneval in September 1897 Wilde counted what each friend had given him: Ross a week, Fothergill six days, 'Reggie gave me three days' (p. 942).
bio_note: Dates (added): born 1869, died 1938, from the editors' first-mention footnote to 'To Reginald Turner', Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000), printed p. 592 n. 1  - '1869-1938. The footnote gives years only; no month or day, so none is recorded. All facts from Holland & Hart-Davis, Complete Letters (2000): 'an old friend of mine who had been very kind to Mr Wilde since his release' and 'the whole of the last week' from Ross to Adela Schuster, 14 Dec. 1900, pp. 1227-1228; night-nursing, delirium restraint, ice-bag, expenses and the 'dear little Jew' remark from Turner's own letters to Ross, [November 1900], pp. 1217-1218; deathbed-presence caption to plate 84 and the Rome inscription caption to plate 89 from the unpaginated plate section; procession and wreath from p. 1222.
